coaching.headline: No fight won in twenty two minutes, and four objectives after minute eighteen fell without a fight at all.
coaching.team: Three of the four lane reads started unfavored: the carry, offlane, and support matchups all ran the enemy's way the whole game, and midlane opened even before swinging to Shinbi late. Only the jungle matchup opened in our favor, and it showed immediately when Rampage got the game's first kill on Scarlett at 2 minutes. The comp brought three physical attackers and two magical to the enemy's four and one, our only healer was Zinx against their Phase, and the team finished with zero anti-heal and zero armor against that physical comp; Serath alone put up 28,926 damage to heroes unchecked. River control ran lopsided across the game, three river fights to their seventeen, one seedling to their two, and Fangtooth went their way three times. The fights that decided the game were taken down bodies or not taken at all: the first at their Fangtooth at 7.5 minutes, lost 0-2 while two teammates stayed back in losing lanes, then the Outer Tower fight at 15.3 minutes lost 0-3 three-on-five, then the Fangtooth fight at 19.4 that opened the door to Orb Prime, and finally a full-strength wipe at their Inner Tower at 21.7 that closed it out. The next-game focus is counting bodies before engaging: a teammate was flagged absent, either pinned in a losing lane or simply unengaged, in four of the game's eight fights, and Murdock alone was caught alone four times before the loss was sealed. Get the group together before the fight starts, not after.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: What actually cost the game? Not the early skirmishes; the 1-1 trade at 2 minutes was close. It was the fights taken down bodies and the ones nobody showed up to. The team never won a fight all game, zero wins against five taken by the opponent, four of them cashed into a tower or objective. After 18 minutes, four objectives in a row, Mini Prime, Genesis Core, Fangtooth, and Orb Prime, fell with nobody on our side even dead beforehand. Nobody was there to contest them, an awareness problem more than a numbers one.
coaching.whatWorked: The one clean win was the jungle matchup. Rampage against Serath opened favored, and it paid off right away with the game's first kill, on Scarlett, at 2 minutes, the only lane read that started ahead of schedule all game.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Legion was flagged absent from four of the game's eight fights, still stuck in a losing lane against Sparrow every time, including the team's first game-defining loss at their Fangtooth, 0-2, at 7.5 minutes. He didn't reach a fight until the final teamfight at their Inner Tower at 21.7 minutes, and was the last of the five caught, at 22.1, just before the tower fell at 22.2. That patience kept his own deaths down to one, but it meant the team fought most of its battles a body light.
perPlayer.3fb86c5f-7d10-4826-b803-b5ed338834c1: Murdock was caught alone four times over the game, by Scarlett or by Serath, more solo catches than the rest of the roster combined, while the enemy lost a player to it just once all game. He was also alive and free to move, not pinned in a losing lane, for three of the fights the team lost as a result, including the 0-3 loss at their Outer Tower at 15.3 minutes. Getting to that fight changes the read from a losing three-on-five to a full five-on-five.
perPlayer.ed629def-5649-47a2-bfd2-1b6d60526ae3: Zinx led the team in wards for the game, 11, and topped it in healing, 12,693, real support production even with zero kills to show for it. The bigger issue was survivability: five of her six deaths came within a minute of an enemy tower or objective falling, a death cadence that ran through the second half of the game against a comp that was four-of-five physical, into which the team brought no armor at all.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Rampage opened the game's best matchup and landed the game's first kill, on Scarlett, at 2 minutes. From there his jungle read went the other way: eight deaths, the most on either team, and six of them came within a minute of an objective or tower falling, Fangtooth twice, the Mini Prime once, four separate towers. Against a comp that was four-of-five physical, he itemized no armor either.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Renna's mid lane against Shinbi started even and slipped to unfavored late, matching her scoreline of four deaths to two kills. She joined most of the team's fights rather than sitting them out, and her only clean solo death was being caught alone by Serath at 11.5 minutes. By the Fangtooth fight at 19.4 minutes her lane had gone from even to losing.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.text: One death in 22 minutes, but Legion was flagged absent, pinned in a losing lane, in four of the game's eight fights.

3fb86c5f-7d10-4826-b803-b5ed338834c1.text: Murdock was caught alone four times, more than the rest of the roster combined, while the enemy lost nobody to it but once all game.

ed629def-5649-47a2-bfd2-1b6d60526ae3.text: Zinx led the team in wards and healing, real support numbers, but six deaths, five of them just before an objective or tower fell, made her the team's most expensive repeat death.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.text: Rampage opened the game's best matchup with the first kill at 2 minutes, then led both teams with eight deaths, six of which handed the enemy an objective or tower within a minute.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.text: Renna's lane went from even to lost across the game, but she was one of the more present players in the team's fights rather than one of the absent ones.

21.7.call: This was the whole squad at full strength, and it still went 1-5 to essentially two enemy heroes, Serath and Sparrow, who chained through the entire lineup. With no armor in the build against their physical comp and no answer for Serath's dive, contesting the Inner Tower here just handed over the last fight of the game; the read needed to be to fall back and force the fight somewhere the dive couldn't chain kills.

15.3.call: Three of us walked into this fight at their Outer Tower with Legion still pinned in a losing lane and Murdock, who was free to leave his own losing lane, not there either. That's a fight taken two bodies light for a tower that wasn't worth it; the call was to wait for the group or skip the tower instead of trading three-on-five numbers with two teammates on the sideline.

19.4.call: Rampage and Zinx took a two-on-two at Fangtooth already an item behind, three items to their four, while three teammates were elsewhere. Losing that fight fed their Inner Tower fall minutes later. On a losing item count, the right read is to disengage and regroup instead of forcing the smaller fight.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Legion built Malady and Deathstalker but missed Vanquisher, the third piece of the meta core; the full core, Malady, Vanquisher, and Deathstalker, wins 56.9% of games. Against Sparrow's ramping damage in a lane he was losing all game, the execute pressure Vanquisher adds against low-health targets was the missing piece.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Legion's loadout runs Vermis as the major, an on-hit anti-tank effect that ramps off landing repeated autos on the same target, paired with Serration and Melting Point to punish low health and heavily armored targets, a natural fit for an auto-attack carry looking to duel a target down over several hits. The trade is that Vermis needs sustained exchanges to pay off, and Legion spent most of the lane phase held back in a losing matchup rather than getting the extended trades that ramp it; a burst-oriented major would ask less patience of a lane that never got room to duel.

3fb86c5f-7d10-4826-b803-b5ed338834c1.build: Murdock had Vanquisher, the execute item that finishes low-health targets, but built Manta Scythe instead of the meta pairing of Lightning Hawk and Imperator. Manta Scythe's bonus damage to isolated targets fits his poke-and-snipe kit on paper, but Murdock was the one repeatedly caught isolated this game rather than punishing the enemy for it. Lightning Hawk and Imperator both add raw power and crit; without them his poke chipped for less at the range where he's supposed to win the trade before the trap and out-range tools ever land.
3fb86c5f-7d10-4826-b803-b5ed338834c1.eternal: Murdock's loadout is the same on-hit package as Legion's, Vermis with Serration and Melting Point, which lines up with his own kit note that his win condition runs through landing repeated hits at range before finishing with the global ultimate. The trade is that Vermis rewards staying in the fight to keep the on-hit stacking, and Murdock's kit read is explicit that he has almost no escape once engaged; leaning into a sustained on-hit package instead of a safer poke-and-disengage major is a bet that he can hold range, which the Scarlett matchup and his four solo deaths this game say he couldn't.

ed629def-5649-47a2-bfd2-1b6d60526ae3.build: Zinx built Crescelia and Timewarp, both ability-haste and mana items that speed up her heal-and-poke rotation, but missed all three of the meta core, Prophecy, Spectra, and Orion. None of those three add armor either, so the team's flagged gap, zero armor into a comp that was four-of-five physical, wasn't something her own item slots were going to fix on their own; it's a build the whole roster shared. What the meta core adds over what she ran is more on-hit and ability-power scaling for her poke, which matters less than the fact that she died six times, five of them right before an enemy tower or objective fell.
ed629def-5649-47a2-bfd2-1b6d60526ae3.eternal: Zinx's loadout is Exarch as the major, which turns her heals and shields into an attack-speed and on-hit-damage buff for whoever she targets, a direct fit for an enchanter whose win condition is keeping a carry alive and empowered through Infuse. The minors, Revelation and Fervour, add more casts and passive team healing on top. The trade is that Exarch's value depends entirely on Zinx surviving to keep casting it; she can't heal herself, and a support pick built around staying in the fight to empower allies is exactly the kind of target a dive threat like Serath is supposed to kill first, which happened six times.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Rampage built Overlord and Rapture, both health-and-sustain items that fit his ramping-regen jungle identity, but skipped Cursed Scroll, the third piece of his meta core. Cursed Scroll is the one item in that trio that carries armor, 50 physical and 30 magical, along with attack speed and health regen; without it Rampage had zero armor against a comp that was four-of-five physical, which matters directly for a jungler whose win condition is out-sustaining a brawl rather than winning it in one burst. Six of his eight deaths this game came within a minute of an objective or tower falling, and more raw health and regen without the armor piece didn't change that math.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Rampage's loadout runs Thraex as the major, which marks the last hero he's autoed for bonus damage dealt and reduced damage taken while the mark holds, paired with Savage Strikes and Ferocity for stacking on-hit damage and attack speed in extended fights, a fit for his own kit note to grow with Behemoth and out-sustain the fight. The trade is that Thraex needs Rampage to survive into the ramp before it pays off, and his own kit read says anti-heal and kiting beat that sustain plan if he's burst down before Behemoth comes online, close to what happened across eight deaths, several of them before the fight had a chance to go long.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Renna built Entropy and Wraith Leggings, both magical-power and ability-haste pieces that fit her zone-based mage kit, but missed Overseer, the third meta-core item. Overseer adds magical penetration and a heal-on-damage passive, sustain that a fragile, zone-reliant mage benefits from once she's committed to a fight from range; without it Renna had less staying power in exchanges that went long, in a mid matchup that was even early and swung unfavored by the late game.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Renna's loadout is Vesh as the major, which turns her ability damage on heroes into a follow-up damage-over-time tick, paired with The Tenth Seal and Mind Rot for extra ultimate power and bonus damage scaled off a target's current health, a fit for a poke-and-zone mage whose combo runs through Mortal Coil and Abyssal Rift chunking from range rather than diving in. The trade is that Vesh's value comes from landing ability hits from a distance and staying alive to let the DoT tick, and Renna's own kit note flags her as fragile and reliant on those zones, exactly the profile that got her caught alone once, by Serath, at 11.5 minutes.

threats: Heal-stacking: Phase. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Enemy is 4/5 physical — a single armor item blunts most of their damage; itemize armor on anyone diveable.
Dive threat on our backline: Serath. Assign peel for the carry and ward the flanks.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Zinx) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

ourKits.combo: Ricochet stun → Bad Medicine zone → Infuse heal an ally → Neural Regenesis revive
ourKits.winCondition: keep an ally alive with Infuse + the revive ult and poke with Ricochet
ourKits.playWith: a carry she can pocket-heal and revive
ourKits.playAgainst: she can't heal herself — dive HER; bait the revive before committing

ourKits.combo: Pounce → Rumble slow → Boulder Throw → Behemoth ult to brawl
ourKits.winCondition: engage with Pounce, grow with Behemoth and out-sustain the fight
ourKits.passive: ramping health regen for jungle sustain
ourKits.playWith: follow-up damage while he front-lines and CCs
ourKits.playAgainst: anti-heal and kiting beat his sustain brawl; burst him before Behemoth

ourKits.combo: Soulfire waves → Mortal Coil pull-zone → Stupor orb → Abyssal Rift zone
ourKits.winCondition: zone a fight with Mortal Coil + ult and chunk from range
ourKits.passive: consumes essences from kills for power
ourKits.playWith: frontline to hold enemies in her zones
ourKits.playAgainst: fragile and reliant on her zones — flank/dive around the telegraphs

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes → Line Tempo wolves → Circle Rhythm shield → All-Kill! wolfpack ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Track and unleash All-Kill! in a grouped fight
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread vs the wolfpack; she's squishy without her shield up

enemyKits.combo: Telekinetic Link an ally → Psychic Flare blind → Energy Lance → Hyperflux buff ult
enemyKits.winCondition: buff a hyper-carry through the Link and Hyperflux for a teamfight
enemyKits.passive: abilities heal her and her linked ally
enemyKits.playWith: the strongest carry to Link and supercharge
enemyKits.playAgainst: kill the linked carry, not Phase; break the link timing

enemyKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
enemyKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
enemyKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
enemyKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up
